instructions: Read each statement and choose how much you agree with it as a description of how you generally feel about yourself. Answer honestly; there are no right or wrong answers.

traits.name: Self-worth
traits.description: Your sense that you matter and have value.

traits.name: Self-acceptance
traits.description: How comfortable you are with who you are, flaws included.

traits.name: Self-respect
traits.description: How well you honour your own needs and boundaries.

traits.name: Confidence
traits.description: How much you trust your abilities and judgement.

traits.name: Self-perception
traits.description: How positively you see your qualities and strengths.

traits.name: Inner voice
traits.description: How kindly you speak to yourself. Higher means a kinder inner voice.

questions.text: On the whole, I am satisfied with myself.
At times I think I am no good at all.
I feel that I have a number of good qualities.
I am able to do things as well as most other people.
I feel I do not have much to be proud of.
I certainly feel useless at times.
I feel that I'm a person of worth, at least on an equal plane with others.
I wish I could have more respect for myself.
All in all, I am inclined to feel that I am a failure.
I take a positive attitude toward myself.
I believe I deserve kindness and respect from others.
My worth does not depend on how well I perform.
I can accept my flaws without being harsh on myself.
I often wish I were a completely different person.
I set boundaries when people treat me poorly.
I keep the promises I make to myself.
I put others' needs before my own, even when it harms me.
I trust my own judgement when making decisions.
I feel comfortable sharing my opinions in a group.
I avoid new challenges because I expect to fail.
I can name things I am genuinely good at.
When I compare myself with others, I usually come out worse.
When I make a mistake, I speak to myself harshly.
I am quick to criticise myself.
I can encourage myself when things get hard.

sources: Items 1-10: Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale. Rosenberg, M. (1965). Society and the Adolescent Self-Image. Princeton University Press. Public domain.
